details: As of July 1, 2026, Binance has ceased new sign-ups, spot trading, deposits, and Earn products for EU users, due to the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. The exchange withdrew its Greek license application on June 24, leaving it without authorization in any EU country. This move significantly impacts the European crypto landscape, as only around 210 out of over 3,000 crypto firms operating in Europe have secured full CASP authorization under MiCA.
title: Binance Exits EU Due to MiCA Regulations

details: Former President Donald Trump's annual financial disclosure, released on Tuesday, revealed over $1.2 billion in earnings from various cryptocurrency ventures in 2025. The report also indicated that Trump holds more than $50 million in Bitcoin. This disclosure highlights the increasing presence and acceptance of cryptocurrencies within mainstream political and financial circles.
title: Trump Discloses Over $1.2 Billion in Crypto Earnings, Holds $50M in Bitcoin

details: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, has adopted a new capital plan that, for the first time, permits the sale of Bitcoin. Proceeds from potential sales could be used to fund the company's USD reserve, support preferred dividends, and finance up to $2 billion in stock buybacks. This represents a significant shift from the company's previous strategy of exclusively accumulating Bitcoin, potentially impacting market sentiment.
title: MicroStrategy's New Capital Plan Allows for Bitcoin Sales

details: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a key indicator of market sentiment, has dropped to a level of 11, indicating "extreme fear" among investors. This decline from 15 the previous day suggests heightened anxiety and reflects turbulent market conditions for cryptocurrencies, particularly Bitcoin. Historically, extreme fear levels can sometimes precede market bottoms, but they also indicate persistent concerns over price stability.
title: Crypto Fear & Greed Index Plunges to 11, Signaling 'Extreme Fear'

details: Bitcoin's price has fallen below the $59,000 mark, with June seeing record outflows from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) totaling $4.5 billion. This significant outflow indicates a waning institutional demand and contributes to the overall downward pressure on Bitcoin's price. The broader cryptocurrency market continues to experience a correction, with Ethereum also breaching the $1,600 level.
title: Bitcoin Falls Below $59K as June ETF Outflows Hit Record $4.5 Billion
